summary: Gifford Pinchot NF summit lookout: 1940 cabin, 1943 26-ft L-4 pole tower, AWS use 1942-43; abandoned in the 1950s. Five foundation blocks remain per Oregon Hikers.

facts.design: 1940 cabin, replaced by a 26-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab (dated 1943 by WillhiteWeb and firelookout.com)
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say abandoned in the 1950s and gone; Oregon Hikers says a tower was destroyed in the 1950s; the Washington lookout list marks it removed. Oregon Hikers reports five foundation blocks remain.

staffing.status: Pete Paladeni manned the lookout around 1935 (WillhiteWeb); no other staffing named in the sources read

access.note: Gifford Pinchot National Forest. WillhiteWeb gives paved access and a hike of almost two miles with a 1,200-foot gain. Oregon Hikers gives 2.6 miles on foot from the Trout Creek Trailhead.

visit.trail_note: No tower stands. Oregon Hikers: 2.6 miles on foot from the Trout Creek Trailhead, which has driving directions. WillhiteWeb: almost 2 miles, 1,200-foot gain.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest

events.note: Pete Paladeni manned the lookout around 1935 (WillhiteWeb); he recalled a little lookout house on the summit
Cabin built on the summit per the register; WillhiteWeb says the lookout inventory has a cabin there in 1940
Aircraft Warning Service use begins; activated March 9, 1942 (Portland Filter Center per weebly list)
Cabin replaced by a 26-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb date it to 1943; the register leaves the date out
Aircraft Warning Service station inactivated October 15, 1943; sleeping quarters and woodshed added with AWS funds; Forest Service kept the site as a fire detection point
Abandoned in the 1950s per the register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb. Only the decade is given; year set to 1950 as a placeholder.
Oregon Hikers says a former lookout tower was destroyed in the 1950s. Conflicts with 'abandoned'. Decade only; year set to 1950 as a placeholder.
Former Fire Lookout Sites registration dated April 7, 2020

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say abandoned in the 1950s. Oregon Hikers says a tower was destroyed in the 1950s. The Washington list says removed. The story reports the abandoned account and notes the destroyed account.
WillhiteWeb gives almost two miles; Oregon Hikers gives 2.6 miles from the Trout Creek Trailhead. Both are reported; the routes may differ.
The register gives the 26-foot pole tower no date. firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb date it to 1943. The story gives 1943 with those two sources.

sources.title: Bunker Hill Lookout in Skamania County

notes_for_editor: Brief's 1940 built event is supported; the 26-foot tower's 1943 date comes from firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb. The register does not date the tower. Height 7.9 m is converted from 26 feet. Sources disagree on how the lookout ended (abandoned vs destroyed). Oregon Hikers is not in the brief's source list; it was found by search and is the only source for the foundation blocks and the 2.6-mile route. WillhiteWeb notes a second former Bunker Hill lookout near the Canada border in the Pasayten Wilderness; that is the Okanogan record. Access set to public from the Forest Service land and trail descriptions; confirm before publishing the access line.
